content: Standard signing-key-rotation pattern uses a key ID (kid) embedded with the signed artifact so the verifier can look up which key produced the signature. Rotation sequence: add new key alongside old (old still signs), cut signing over to new key while old key remains valid for verification only, then remove old key from the verifier once all artifacts signed with it have aged past their max validity window (e.g., token TTL or, for unsubscribe links, the realistic maximum time an email link stays clickable). HMAC (HS256-style) rotation is harder than asymmetric because the same shared secret must be distributed to every verifier simultaneously or multiple secrets tried in sequence during the transition.
